routes.description: Establish that the named scientific, moral, historical, experiential, and aesthetic considerations form a coherent cumulative case that favors Christian theism over skeptical agnosticism despite the absence of demonstrative certainty.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the considerations jointly support an intelligent and personal creator, connect that conclusion specifically to Christianity, and remain comparatively credible after objections concerning divine power, suffering, historical reliability, and alternative explanations.

motionBridge.description: Show that fine-tuning, morality, resurrection, revelation, and beauty collectively raise the comparative plausibility of Christian theism above skeptical agnosticism.

centralBridges.description: Connect cosmic order and life-permitting structure to purposeful intelligence while explaining their compatibility with divine freedom and orderly creation.
Connect moral awareness, altruism, and value-laden experience to a personal and morally significant God rather than merely a deistic cause.
Supply a defensible transition from generic theism to Christianity through Jesus, resurrection claims, and the cumulative interpretation of Christian sources.
Explain why evolutionary suffering, natural evil, source criticism, and naturalistic mechanisms do not overturn the cumulative inference.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Justify rational commitment on convergent but noncoercive evidence without requiring mathematical proof or certainty.
Explain how personal revelation and aesthetic experience may provide additional access to divine reality alongside public argument.

routes.description: Establish that the named considerations remain ambiguous, underdetermined, or counterbalanced, so they do not warrant preferring Christian theism to a skeptical agnostic position that preserves uncertainty while taking the evidence seriously.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if alternative explanations, internal tensions, adverse evidence, and limits on public or historical justification prevent the cumulative case from identifying the Christian God with sufficient comparative force.

motionBridge.description: Show that the motion's considerations do not discriminate strongly enough in favor of Christian theism to displace skeptical agnosticism.

centralBridges.description: Require a sufficiently intelligible and testable conception of God before observations can count specifically as evidence for Christian theism.
Test fine-tuning against rival creator hypotheses, divine omnipotence, cosmic scale, and the comparative evidence supplied by evolutionary suffering.
Require resurrection and scriptural claims to withstand source criticism, legendary-development explanations, and uncertainty about testimony.
Determine whether morality, revelation, beauty, and the other considerations remain too equivocal for strong confidence in their theological interpretation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Distinguish experiences that may justify belief for a recipient from evidence capable of supporting the motion publicly.
Preserve the importance of investigating Christianity while separating practical or intellectual significance from comparative truth support.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Cosmic Order, and Divine Creative Power
sections.rationale: This issue tests a principal inference from life-permitting physical structure to intelligence, including whether fine-tuning is expected under an omnipotent creator and whether rival creator or natural explanations limit Christian specificity.

sections.title: Morality, Evolutionary Suffering, and the Character of God
sections.rationale: Moral awareness and altruism are offered as routes toward a personal God, while scriptural tension and extensive animal suffering test whether the observed moral order fits a loving Christian creator.

sections.title: Resurrection and the Historical Reliability of Christian Sources
sections.rationale: The resurrection supplies the most direct bridge from generic theism to Christianity, making testimony, Gospel development, corroboration, priors, martyrdom traditions, and alternative historical explanations central to the motion.

sections.title: Revelation, Public Evidence, and Rational Commitment
sections.rationale: This issue determines what level and kind of evidence can rationally support commitment, and whether personal revelation can contribute to the comparative case beyond providing private justification to its recipient.

sections.title: Beauty, Transcendence, and the Cumulative Case
sections.rationale: Aesthetic experience bears on transcendence while admitting evolutionary and non-theistic interpretations; its role also frames whether several individually uncertain considerations can jointly favor belief or instead counsel agnostic restraint.
